# Bard's Tale XR

> A browser-based, Three.js/WebXR dungeon RPG inspired by classic first-person party-based fantasy games. The project must remain playable on desktop without a headset, support WebXR emulation for development, and eventually run on standalone XR hardware. Preserve data-driven gameplay rules and keep XR presentation separate from game state and combat logic.

## Read first

Before changing code:

1. Read this file.
2. Read every linked local document relevant to the requested task.
3. Inspect the current modules named by those docs before proposing implementation.
4. Make the smallest change that satisfies the request.
5. Do not refactor unrelated systems.
6. Run required tests and `npm run build`.
7. Report files changed, validation results, manual test steps, and known limitations.

When a local repository implementation conflicts with an external example or generic framework advice, the local project implementation wins.

## Project stack

- Vanilla JavaScript ES modules
- Vite
- Three.js
- WebXR Device API
- Web Audio API
- XR Blocks-style modular architecture
- Desktop browser mode plus WebXR/emulator testing

Do not introduce React, Unity, a second renderer, a second XR bootstrap, a new game engine, or broad dependencies without explicit approval.

## Architecture

Read these before work that affects their area:

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): Entry points, module boundaries, game-loop states, XR bootstrapping, world/UI conventions.
- [Agent workflow](docs/agent-workflow.md): Required inspect → plan → implement → validate process.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): Test commands, development checks, build checks, and regression rules.

## XR and scenes

- [XR scene guide](docs/antigravity-xr-scene-guide.md): Scene lifecycle, disposal, scale, comfort, interaction fallback, and performance requirements.
- [XR Blocks reference](docs/xrblocks-reference.md): Curated XR Blocks guidance and integration cautions.
- [XR Blocks source index](docs/xrblocks-source-index.md): Official docs/sample links; inspect only sources relevant to the assigned task.

XR rules:

- Preserve desktop keyboard/mouse fallback for every feature.
- Controller input is required for XR interactions; hand tracking is optional.
- Do not move the WebXR camera directly.
- Use existing XR rig, locomotion, and game-state abstractions.
- One Three.js unit equals one meter.
- Prefer discrete grid movement and snap turns for dungeon exploration.
- Avoid forced camera motion, flashing, sustained awkward head rotation, and expensive per-frame allocations.
- Scene modules must clean up event listeners, timers, geometry, materials, textures, audio, and render targets they own.

## Gameplay data

- [Data registries](docs/data-registry.md): Canonical IDs, source provenance, normalization, and lookup rules.
- [Combat system](docs/combat-system.md): Canonical combat pipeline and immutable runtime state rules.
- [Combat sandbox](docs/combat-sandbox.md): Developer-only deterministic test harness and panel usage.
- [Item system](docs/item-system.md): Item registry, instances, equipment, activation, and deferred mechanics. Read this before item work.

Authoritative source modules:

- [Monster registry](src/data/MonsterDatabase.js): Immutable canonical monster definitions, IDs 0–126.
- [Spell registry](src/data/SpellDatabase.js): Immutable canonical spell definitions, IDs 0–104.
- [Item registry](src/data/ItemDatabase.js): Canonical item definitions. Do not alter source data unless the task explicitly requests it.
- [Combat contracts](src/core/combat/CombatTypes.js)
- [Monster factory](src/core/combat/MonsterFactory.js)
- [Monster action resolver](src/core/combat/MonsterEffectResolver.js)
- [Encounter state](src/core/combat/EncounterState.js)
- [Combat event applier](src/core/combat/CombatEventApplier.js)
- [Combat sandbox](src/core/combat/CombatSandbox.js)

Data rules:

- Numeric source IDs are immutable provenance IDs.
- Stable slugs are permanent runtime and save-game keys.
- Static registry definitions must remain deeply immutable.
- Store mutable state—HP, statuses, buffs, charges, identification, equipment—in runtime instances/state only.
- Do not use item or spell display names for rules dispatch. Use IDs, slugs, typed effects, or source metadata.
- Preserve unknown source behavior as explicit `unimplemented` output rather than inventing rules.
- Do not merge the new combat/item pipeline into legacy `CombatEngine.js` without an approved integration plan.

## Developer tooling

- The combat sandbox is development-only.
- The combat sandbox panel is gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.
- Use it to validate monsters, spells, combat events, summons, and later item usage.
- Do not expose debug APIs or panels in production builds.

## Required validation

After relevant code changes, run:

```bash
node src/core/utils/DiceAndFactory.test.js
node src/core/utils/SpellDatabase.test.js
node src/core/utils/MonsterEffectResolver.test.js
node src/core/utils/CombatEventApplier.test.js
node src/core/utils/CombatSandbox.test.js
npm run build
```

If item work has added item tests, also run:

```bash
node src/core/utils/ItemDatabase.test.js
node src/core/utils/InventoryState.test.js
node src/core/utils/ItemEffectResolver.test.js
```

For UI/XR changes, also run:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Manually verify desktop controls. When relevant, test using the Immersive Web Emulator. Do not claim Quest performance, comfort, controller ergonomics, or hand tracking is validated without a real headset.

## Constraints

- Do not modify canonical monster, spell, or item source records unless explicitly told to change source data.
- Do not modify `CombatEngine.js`, `CombatArena.js`, XR systems, game loop, or player-facing UI as collateral damage.
- Plan before broad integration or refactoring.
- Keep development-only code behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.
- Use original visual assets, audio, maps, text, and UI art for publicly distributed builds.
- Keep proprietary/source-derived reference data separate from original presentation assets.

## Task plan template

Before implementing a substantial task, report:

- Goal
- Relevant docs read
- Existing modules inspected
- Files to create/change
- Public APIs affected
- Desktop controls and XR controls
- Runtime/data ownership
- Cleanup/disposal plan
- Performance risks
- Test and manual verification plan
